Because one of the specialities of the Serb military police was to beat people on the soles of their feet so that one couldn't run, one couldn't flee, one couldn't walk. And for about a month, what little food he was entitled to had to be brought to him because he was prostrate.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Was he beaten inside the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: He was brought in that bad shape, but he was also put in solitary confinement. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Do you know a Kresimir Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: Kresimir Martinovic. I knew him personally. He was a TV repairman, and he had found a job in Zagreb, come back to fetch his wife, and was captured by the Serb police especially because he knew Velibor Ostojic. That is what he told us when he recovered a little. And his bodyguards beat him so badly, so terribly that his facial traits were completely changed. And people also tried to treat him with those cold compresses, and he also disappeared after a short while.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: And do you also know a Nail Hodzic detained at KP Dom whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: Nail Hodzic used to work for the same company as I did for a while and then moved over to Focatrans and drove a bus for that company. But at the same time, according to some information that I learnt there -- I had no previous knowledge about that -- that he used to be a treasurer for the SDA. He was also beaten, and yet only a few days later he was taken away and never returned. After the beating he was taken away. Ten days later he was taken away and never came back.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Did you see any injuries from that beating or just heard about it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: In Room 12 -- no, sorry. In Room 11. And it was the same entrance, the same doorway, so that usually at mealtime we would go to another building, and that was our only opportunity to communicate with -- to communicate with the guards. The guards would say, "Room 12 goes for a meal with room such-and-such," and then, "Room such-and-such goes with room such-and-such," because that was the best way they could control the discipline and our conduct in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: So you didn't see his injuries. You heard about it through other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: Heard, I heard it from him, because we knew one another quite well.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: And Omer Mujezinovic, did you know him while you were at the KP Dom? Omer Mujezinovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: And Habib Subasic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: Yes. Him I --

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Was he beaten whilst you were at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: He came beaten. He was badly -- they beat him badly first and then they brought him. But then, and why I don't know, he spent quite a long time in solitary confinement. Excuse me. Because many of those who were beaten lacked courage to say who had beaten them, who had done it to them. In the camp, in the prison, don't ask -- don't ask from people too much. Don't insist on people telling you who beat them.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: And Zulfo Veiz, did you know him whilst you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: I used to know him before that.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Whilst you were at the KP Dom, did you know whether he was beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: He was beaten when he was brought there together with Munib Veiz but less than Munib Veiz. And he was in the same department where I was, that is, in Room 15, which had two wings. And he also frequently communicated with some of the Serb police because whilst a civilian, he also served as a policeman. Sometime around the 20th or the 21st, but I'm positive more that I'm telling you now it was the 2100 hours, and we were smoking some grass or other, and he looked through the window - it was dark - and he said, "Here they come to take me away," and that's how it was. He sensed that he would be taken away, that he would be the one that they would take away out of 30 of us.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Which month was this? You said the 20th or the 21st.

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: The 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: You say the 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: The 21st of August. The 20th or the 21st of August.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: And you were in the same room as him, and he said that he was going to be taken out. This is Room 15? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: It was the department of Room 15, and there was one big room with some 30 beds and a smaller room with -- with 8 beds. And there was also a third room, which was sort of an anteroom, with about 10 benches, and there was also a small area in front of the lavatory.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: And you said, I think, at 9.00 he was taken out of your room. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: Yes, it is. At 9.00 in the evening, at 2100.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: And who was he taken out by?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: I-- was it Obrenovic? And I really don't know them well. Pljevaljcic, Obrenovic, Kali [phoen], Ivanovic and so on. I can't really remember who it was. But I fled immediately from that anteroom in which we were when they came after him, and he said, "Here they come to take me away," and I went to my room so that I did not see who that was. But next day they asked not me, others, they asked, "Where's Zulfo?" And the answer was, "He's been sent to another camp."

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Since that day that he was taken out of that room, has he ever been seen again, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: That same evening, ten minutes later, one could hear screams, cries of pain, beating, blows, and we were unfortunate enough to be able to see directly the room in which this was going on, this beating and killing went on.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Which room was this in, which building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: It was on the ground floor of the administrative building. If you look from Room 15, straight ahead -- you see straight ahead where roughly is that office with the darkened window panes.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: This beating and screaming, how long did that last for, how many minutes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: From half an hour to an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: After that beating and screaming had stopped, did you hear anything else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't, but that was one of the last things. But the things that I'll tell you now, they were about -- it happened three or four times a week, usually when they would be taken away as of 6.00 and then a beating would ensue, blows. And you can believe me when I say that I took this sponge from the pillow to plug my ears and then put that pillow over my head just so as not to die because of those screams, because of those cries of pain, because of those sobs which resounded so loudly through the night.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Where were these beatings taking place? In the same place where Zulfo Veiz was or in some other place?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: All of the beatings took place on the ground floor of the administrative building. Almost all of them. But from inmates, from the detainees, I also heard that it also took place in special rooms which were used during that Yugoslavia to beat people; that is, in those rooms, there were also beatings. But what went on in this part, this part which we could directly see from our dormitory, not even a man with a heart of steel, I think, would be able to keep his sanity after hearing all those screams.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: About how many weeks did this continue for, these beatings in this building? You say about three or four times a week people were taken out and beaten. For how many weeks did this occur?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: Well, I should say about two months, close to two months. But not every day. But it would happen twice a week, once a week, three times a week, and it went on for about two months. It wasn't evenly distributed. I suppose it depended on the selection of people who were to be killed.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: And which two-month period was this whilst you were there? Was it your last two months, your first two, or the middle two?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: That was roughly the end of July, end of August. I think that is -- I think that Veiz was around the 20th, 21st of August.

utterances.speaker: THE DOCTOR WHEN MY
utterances.text: Are you 100 per cent sure about these dates?

utterances.speaker: FWS-86
utterances.text: Ninety per cent. After all this time, after all this time, I cannot be 100 per cent sure. But my rough estimate is that it was late June, late August, the 20th, 21st of August, and Veiz was the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that I have about 20 more minutes and I think now might be a good time to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now until 9.30 in the morning. If there are any matters to be dealt with that will take any time, we should deal with them in the morning, that is, matters arising out of the discussions this morning. If you've got anything resolved, just let us know. Otherwise, we'll deal with them and get them out of the way before we proceed with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
